description:
The Abyssal War
v0.9.2 - swarm doctrine - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download

AbyssalWar-0.9.2.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves from 0.8 and 0.9 carry on; removing the mod mid-war breaks the save.

What it is

The Threat (vanilla's abyssal fabricator swarm) colonises the fringe of the sector, grows, and invades the core worlds
Its colonies are real markets with a real economy. You beat it by starving, bombing and invading them, not by killing fleets
The NPC factions fight it on their own. You run your own colonies' war from one intel screen (The Abyssal War)
Standalone. LunaLib optional. Nexerelin compatible. Safe to add mid-save

How a game goes

At game start a hidden fringe system is seeded with several Threat colonies ("hives"). Nobody knows
They grow, spread to neighbouring systems and scout the core. When they can afford a strike that beats what they saw, they attack
A faction whose world is struck mobilises: war economy, patrols, scouts, one big attack fleet. Factions find hives only by flying into their systems
You find hives the same way: fly into the system, or own a colony next door. Found hives appear on the board; the map hides the rest
Once you have colonies, press Mobilise on the board. Your colonies bank hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, and you spend them on orders
A hive dies when its strata (below) reach zero: bomb it from orbit, land marines, or cut off what feeds it. Kill every hive and the war ends
The core holds for years on its own and usually loses without you

The Threat, explained

Strata is a hive's one number. It is the colony's ground defence, its hit points and its troops at once. Fight it on the ground or bomb it from orbit, and the number goes down. Below each size's threshold the colony drops a size; at zero it is destroyed
Each size needs twice the strata of the last, so a size 8 hive is a fortress and a size 2 seed is nothing
Strata is also its fleets. A hive has no standing garrison. When attacked, or to strike, it turns strata into ships ("budding"); when the ships come home it turns them back into strata ("absorbing"). A hive that buds a defence fleet has that much less on the ground
Reclaimed hulls. The swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken; a fleet budded there includes those hulls, with Threat weapons, beside its own ships. A wreck also adds strata to the world
The Fabrication Core is the industry that makes strata. It needs metals and fuel, more of each the bigger the colony. Both met in full: the hive grows a size at a time. Short: it holds. Starved: it loses strata daily and shrinks a size at a time until it is gone
Hives import from each other like any market. Blockade a hive (hold its orbit with warships) and it imports nothing; only its own mines, refineries and fuel plants still feed its Core. Saturation bombardment disrupts those for a year
A hive's accessibility is how much strata stands nearby ("swarm density"). Dense systems grow; an isolated hive starves
Hives move strata between systems: back-line worlds bud fleets that fly to the front and are absorbed there. A world under attack pulls strata in. The hive's best mine, refinery and fuel plant never give strata away below their own size
A strike is strata too. The hive stages strata at its front worlds, grows them toward size 8, then buds the mass as one strike sized to beat the defence its scouts saw
Over your world the strike's ships break up into troops and land. Landed strata never come home
Occupation. The swarm never takes a human world. Each district its army holds lets it eat one industry: the industry stops working, is consumed over its build time and is removed. What it eats becomes strata: troops while the fight is on, then Infestation Swarms in orbit once every district is held. With nothing left to eat the army lifts off and looks for the next world

Hulls consumed by the swarm

A hive's Core fed in full: metals 3 of 3, fuel 1 of 1, 600 strata a month, the next size in 36 days.

The same hive blockaded: nothing docks, the Core gets nothing, it loses a size in 24 days.

Killing a hive

Find it: fly into the system. The Threat tab lists every found system nearest first, with what your last scout saw there and how old that is. Scout sends a scout from the board; Map shows the system
Starve it: blockade the orbit, saturation-bomb its mine, refinery or fuel plant, or kill the hive those imports come from. A seed hive dies on blockade alone
Bomb it: tactical bombardment from the dock razes strata for fuel. The hive buds ships from its strata to stop you; beat them first
Invade it: Ground operations at the dock lands all or half your marines with heavy armaments. The front fights the strata standing and keeps fighting after you leave; Push or Hold it from the board, Reinforce it, Recall evacuates it
Or do it all from the board: Attack on a system's row raises a fleet at your chosen colony, sized by the Fleet lever against the swarms seen there, carrying fuel and marines by the levers, and holds the system for the Days lever. It blockades, bombs while it has fuel, lands its marines on arrival and comes home when both are spent
Its size on the board is what your last scout saw. Nothing about a hive is live

The Threat tab: the swarm's fronts on five human worlds, and every found system nearest first with the last scout's note.

A hive system under attack: its worlds bud fleets out of their strata.

Defending your worlds

A colony's defence is its ground defences manned by marines, plus its spare marines armed with heavy armaments. No marines, no defence: a colony fights with what is in its stockpile
Marines arm over days, take losses daily while a front stands, and gain veterancy. Heavy armaments are burned per marine per day
The fight is one line. Each side pushes with its strength; the net moves the line; a district changes hands when it moves far enough. The board reads it from your side: gaining, grinding, losing
Push spends cover to move the line; Hold regrows cover. A dug-in force breaks under enough weight; an outnumbered push still gains, slower
Each district the swarm holds is an industry it is eating. Take the district back and the industry rebuilds from where it was. Finish eating and it is gone for good
Every front row says what is next (Objective), when (ETA) and when it ends (Victory). Hover for the figures each side needs
While the swarm holds the orbit the colony cannot dock anything; relief convoys wait at the jump point

A front on Haven: who holds what, what each side needs, what is next and when.

A colony under occupation: Farming and Mining being eaten, Ground Defenses rebuilding after its district was retaken.

Your war board

Mobilise puts every colony of yours on War Footing: a market condition that demands hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, so your industries bank them as the colony's stockpile. The stockpile is the reserve the board spends
Domain table: one row a colony with its stockpile, its fleet on station and its status. Levers above it, one per good: None / Med / Max is nothing, half or all of what the colony can spare
Deploy raises a fleet from a colony's hulls at the Fleet lever and sends it where you say. Transfer moves stock between your worlds by convoy. Recall brings a fleet home with what it carries. Attack (Threat tab) sends a fleet at a hive system
Every fleet and convoy pays fuel for the passage and burns supplies while out. It turns home when supplies run out, and its row says why
Call for aid on a world under attack: a toggle per good. Factions with a surplus post offers; Accept, Dismiss or Cancel. Their asks of you show the exact figure, the standing it pays and the ETA; Send or ignore
Defend an ally's orbit for 30 / 90 / 180 days, or send any good to any faction; standing on arrival, one rate either way
Outpost: dock at any uncolonised world to build one. Storage, refit, a base of your own
Nothing of yours moves unless you order it. No order of yours is refused
Every other mobilised faction has a tab: its worlds, fronts, fleets and requests, read the same way

Your tab: three factions answering Arkoman's call for marines, two fronts, and your Domain with its levers and orders.

The sector

A faction mobilises when one of its worlds is struck, never before. Its colonies bank the same reserves yours do
It attacks with one grand fleet: half its navy and every marine and fuel unit its bases can spare, to the nearest hive it outweighs. It bombs and lands until the hive is gone, moves to the next it can reach, and comes home when its holds run dry
Factions aid each other through the same asks and offers you see, their own colonies first
Every strike, grand fleet, convoy and scout is a real fleet you can meet, intercept or fight beside
Kill every hive and every faction stands down

Fog of war

No radar on either side. A hive is found when a ship sees it and gets home
Patrols on both sides. One that cannot outrun a strike dies with its warning
The board shows what your scouts reported and how old it is. The map veils what you have not found
The swarm only strikes worlds its own scouts have charted

Start your way

Default: a hive seeded on the fringe at game start, striking once it can pay
Chill: wake it after the Abyssal questline, or when your colony reaches size 6
Instant War: a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle

The settings menu (LunaLib, Shift+F2) holds the knobs that matter; the rest live in [tt]data/config/settings.json[/tt].

Changelog

0.9.2 - swarm doctrine

Spoiler
Threat fleets fight by what they carry, and big swarms carry fabricators again. Saves from 0.9 carry on: fleets already flying get their fabricators on first load.

Battle doctrine by composition
A Threat fleet with no fabricator or hive in the battle attacks as a swarm: every combat unit aggressive, never backing off, never pulling out to vent, on search and destroy. Before, such a fleet had no orders and ended every battle pinned on its own edge
A fleet with a fabricator or hive deployed defends it, as vanilla
Swarm Doctrine, Swarm Personality (aggressive or reckless), Swarm Never Vents and Swarm Engagement Range (LunaLib)

Fabricators
A budded swarm (Defense and Shifting Swarms, occupation garrisons) carries one fabricator per 1,200 fleet points, at most 3, as its flagship. A fabricator is 600 FP of the fleet. A strike that musters such a swarm keeps its fabricator
Fleets already flying trade their smallest plain Threat hulls for the fabricators their size earns, fleet points unchanged. Converted hulls, hives and overseers are never traded
Fabricator Threshold (FP) and Fabricators Per Fleet (LunaLib)

Hive military options
Raids and bombardment of a hive close only while the swarm holds its orbit, and the menu lists every fleet holding it, so Engage can always reach what closes them. A garrison from a neighbouring moon no longer closes bombardment while the menu says there are no nearby fleets
The bombard tooltip shows both sides' fleet points while the orbit is held

0.9.1 - reclaimed hulls

Spoiler
The swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Saves from 0.9.0 carry on: on first load every hive world of size 5 or more gets a few hulls to start with.

Converted hulls
45 vanilla warships, frigate to capital (carriers included; no phase, civilian, module or unique hulls) have a Threat version, "<Hull> (Converted)": Threat sprite and engines, the automated, Threat and fragment swarm hullmods, unboardable. Fleet points, ordnance and slots are the original's
107 loadouts from vanilla's own variants, with Threat weapons in the mounts: mass drivers and the Neoferric Quadcoil in ballistic mounts, Voltaic Cannon and Voidblaster in energy, Neutron Torpedoes, Kinetic Fragments and Swarm Launchers in missile, Voltaic Discharge for point defence. Large energy, large missile and ballistic point-defence mounts keep the original weapon. Ordnance points are not a limit
The Threat's battle coordination counts them as combat units. Vanilla's own abyss fleets never use them
Converted Hulls (LunaLib) turns them off; read at game launch

The reclaimed-hull ledger
Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken, by type. A hull is in one place: on a ledger, or in a fleet
A battle the swarm wins books every hull the losers lost - yours included - to the winning swarm's world, or the nearest hive. Off-screen fights count too: ships the swarm destroys out of a fleet are booked by name; a route's or an expedition's losses are booked by type from the losing faction's known ships, cheaper types more often
Every hull taken adds half its fleet points as strata at the world. The swarm's own dead are not taken
A fleet budded or built at a world takes its converted share from that world's ledger. A world with no hulls of a class buds Threat units instead, so a young hive that has won nothing has none. Scouts and patrols never carry them
A converted hull absorbed back into a world goes back on the ledger; one destroyed, or landed as troops, is gone

Fleets
Host, Vanguard and Battery swarms spend 10-15 of 100 fleet points on converted hulls, Hunter packs 10 on converted frigates; Tide and Scout carry none
New Reclaimed archetype: overseers herding converted hulls of every class, 65 of 100, in the strike and garrison pools

Debug
Reclaimed Swarm (LunaLib, debug section): once per toggle-on, seeds every hive world's ledger with Reclaimed Seed FP of shapes and buds a Reclaimed swarm of Reclaimed Swarm FP from the hive nearest you, placed beside your fleet with orders to intercept it. Turn it off afterward

0.9.0 - strata are the Threat

Spoiler
The Threat is rebuilt around one number. Before, a hive was a vanilla-style colony with batteries, a military organ, a standing garrison of Defense Swarms and a supplies upkeep. Now a hive is its strata, and everything it does is strata changing form. Saves from 0.8.2 load and carry on (see the end).

Strata
A hive's strata is its ground defence, its hit points and its troops in one number, and its size is read off it: each size needs twice the strata of the last (400 at size 1). Strata lost on the ground or to bombardment lower the number; below the size's threshold the colony shrinks a size; at zero it is destroyed
Gone with it: hive Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, the Swarm Nexus, Bastion and Command, return fire on landings, drop losses, fortification raids, and the hive's supplies upkeep. A hive has nothing to raid
Nothing decays. A hive keeps what it has until something takes it

The Fabrication Core
The Core is the one industry that matters. It turns metals and fuel into strata daily, at a rate set by the colony's size, and demands more of each the bigger the colony (metals at size, fuel at size minus two)
Both inputs met in full: the hive grows, a size at a time. Either short: it holds. Both starved: it loses strata daily and drops a size at a time until it dies
Inputs come from the hive's own mines, refineries and fuel plants and from imports off other hives. A hive industry produces at its size
Blockade (hostile warships holding the orbit) cuts imports to nothing. Saturation bombardment disrupts an industry for a year, so bombing a hive's only fuel plant starves every hive that imports from it
Accessibility is swarm density: strata standing in and near the system. An isolated hive starves on its own; a dense cluster thrives
The Hive Vitality tooltip on a hive's colony screen is the readout: strata and the next size's threshold, inputs met, density or blockade, growth or days to the next size lost

Budding and absorbing
A hive has no standing fleets. It buds ships out of its strata when a hostile fleet holds its orbit, to strike, to shift or to seed, and absorbs them back when the job is done, one ship a tick with the break-up animation on the map
Absorb a fleet and the colony grows by that strata; bud one and it shrinks. A fleet is strata in space. Bombing a hive before it buds leaves it less to bud with
Budding and absorbing run at the world's flow (a fixed amount a day, more at big worlds), so a big fleet takes days to raise
Over an enemy world the swarm's ships break up into troops: a landing is strata on the ground, sized to overrun the defence, and never returns

Strata on the move
The shift: a world that needs strata (under attack, or at the front) is answered by the quiet world of another system that can give the most, which buds a fleet that flies there and is absorbed. Pressing, the hive shifts forward; consolidating, back toward its densest system
A world under attack pulls strata into its system; a system under attack never gives any away
Forward staging: while the hive saves for a campaign it fills its staging worlds toward size 8, then buds the mass as the strike. Strikes bud at every giver in parallel and gather at the staging system, the richest back-line worlds drawn down first
Critical producers keep their size: the sole largest mine, refinery or fuel plant gives nothing below its own size to a strike or a shift, since every importer's supply is read off the largest source. Its own defence may still spend everything
A shift books its passage fuel before it sails. Seeding a new world is strata in flight: the seed lands as a small colony and grows on its Core

Occupation, not conquest
The swarm never takes a human world. Its army on the ground holds districts; each district held lets it eat one industry. An eaten industry stops working at once, is consumed over its own build time (Mining 60 days, Orbital Works 150) and is then removed from the colony. Military structures are eaten last
What it eats becomes strata: troops to the front while districts are contested, and once every district is held a pool that buds Infestation Swarms over the world. A quiet occupation's swarms are reabsorbed; a station over the front draws the next strike
Take a district back and its industry is released and rebuilds from where it was eaten (it shows Rebuilding). The swarm claims the easiest to eat next; defenders reclaim military first
Nothing left to eat: the army lifts off and the swarm picks another world. Its final objective on a world reads Consume; yours on a hive reads Extermination
On the colony screen a claimed industry is tinted with the swarm's icon and a Consumed countdown; the dock is locked while the swarm holds the orbit

The line
One front line replaces the counter-attack cadence. Each side's pressure is its strength; the net moves the line; a district changes hands when it moves far enough. State reads from your side: gaining, grinding, losing, plus entrenched, dug in, holding, breaking, retreating, overrun
Push or Hold (Dig in is now Hold). Push spends cover to move the line, Hold regrows it; pressure breaks cover, so a dug-in force is breakable under enough weight and an outnumbered push gains ground in proportion. Ground taken is kept when you switch
Manned defences: a colony's ground defence counts only with marines to man it and takes losses like them. A colony with no marines defends with nothing
AI fronts push only while pushing moves the line, and hold a stance ten days before changing it
Fronts table: Force in each side's colour, State, Held (districts), Stance, Losses, ETA, Objective (the next district or industry), Arms, Victory, Space. The row tooltip is one line per fact: control of the district, each side's figure and what it needs, attrition, arming pace

Grand fleets (NPC offence)
Each faction attacks with one grand fleet. It musters half the faction's navy (floored and capped) at the base nearest the nearest known hive, loads every marine, armament and fuel unit its base and donors can spare, and sails on hulls, passage and the cruise's supplies
At the nearest hive it outweighs it fights what holds the orbit, razes strata with its fuel, lands its marines and stays until the hive is gone, then moves to the next hive it can reach, else home. A beaten fleet turns home and waits before trying again
The council's sized sieges, hunts, bombing plays and forward bases are gone. Forward bases are off by default and none are founded
Relief goes where the swarm is: a relief over a quiet world moves to its owner's nearest invaded world it can outweigh, or to where you are fighting
A faction tops up its own colonies from sibling surplus before asking the sector; all faction-to-faction aid goes through the asks and answers on the boards, free of standing between NPCs

Your board: levers and orders
The Min / Med / Max ladders are gone. One lever a good above each table (Fuel, Supplies, Marines, Arms, Hulls, Fleet): None / Med / Max is nothing, half or all of what the source colony can spare
Domain table: Colony, Size, Military, Def, Hulls, Marines, Arms, Fuel, Supplies, Strikes, Status, Fleet, Actions. Status is what the world needs. One button a row: Deploy (a fleet, with the Fleet lever set) or Transfer (a convoy), and Recall
Deploy raises a fleet from a colony's free hulls (the nearest colony with hulls when the row's has none), loads the levers' share of its stock, and sails where you say; Redeploy moves it on. Inside the colony's own system it is never refused for supplies. Fleets are capped at 2,400 FP each; a bigger force sails as several
Attack (Threat tab, each system's row): Colony picks the colony it sails from (your staging base by default), Fleet sizes it against the swarms seen there, Days sets how long it holds each world (60 / 120 / 240). The colony levers load its fuel and marines. At the target it blockades, bombs while it has fuel, lands its marines on arrival, and comes home when both are spent
Fronts: one stance button (Push / Hold), Reinforce at the levers, Recall sails the evacuation convoy at once, Request on your own world under a Threat army
Defend an ally's orbit for 30 / 90 / 180 days (Days lever), priced on the term; a defence fleet earns standing by its fleet points
Your orders are never gated by a front, a spare cap or a range: distance costs time and fuel. Nothing of yours moves unordered (no automatic convoys from your colonies)
Fleet rows show an ETA while sailing and days left once arrived; a Returning row says why; convoy rows show a blockade hold; scouts and patrols show in the fleets table

Requests and aid
The mission board is gone. Call for aid with a toggle per good (Fuel, Supplies, Marines, Arms, Hulls, Fleet) on a world under attack; factions look at standing calls daily
Offers come only from colonies with a real surplus, sized to what that colony can spare (its own siege bank held back), never to your need. Accept, Dismiss or Cancel; a faction busy with the war answers slower; a donor that needs the goods withdraws. No table shows while no offer stands
NPC tabs share the Requests table. A faction's ask of you shows the exact figure, sized to what you can field, the standing it pays and the ETA. Send or ignore. Left a few days, friendly factions answer it and the row logs who did
Standing: one rate either way, on a curve, hulls priced above armaments. Aid any non-hostile faction to raise standing. A transfer of your own landing at your own world notifies like aid
Strike contracts, the Hunt order and the Hive systems in reach table are gone

Convoys, fleets, performance
Convoys pay fuel and supplies for the voyage, yours included, billed on the hulls they sail with. A blockaded colony sends none, and a convoy to one waits at the jump point until the orbit clears
One fleet: every force sails as fleets of up to 2,400 FP (knob) in place of a dozen 300 FP fleets, both sides. Idle swarm fleets over a quiet world are reabsorbed
The LunaLib menu lists 63 knobs with a tangible effect in place of 439
Marines are crew first: a colony's defence counts the marines manning its ground defence, then the rest as armed troops

Information
The Threat tab shows what your scouts know, nothing live: Distance first, Strikes, Activity, Supply, a Notes cell from the last report ("Size 8 fuel production", "Strike staging", "Starving") with its age, and Scout, Map and Attack on every row. Mass, state, Reach and Flow are gone
Scouts range on their fuel and sweep found hives their faction has no report of; a lost scout is logged. The map veils found hives too (debug mode unveils it and adds a Debug tab of the swarm's plans)

Notices and the colony screen
Technical reports only: the war comms, the omens, hive size-change notices and AI fleet announcements are gone. Notices carry the Abyssal War intel tag and are not Major events
A destroyed colony's card names the destroyer. Beachhead Overrun on your world plays the mission-complete chime. The Ground War condition icon is gone from the colony screen; no Cancel upgrade on a held card
The hive's colony screen reads the strata: no Spaceport line, no stability lines, no human demands; the Hive Vitality tooltip is the readout
Player outposts: the dock offers vanilla's storage, ship transfer and refit, plus Decommission. Never mind on a hive bombardment returns to the mod's menu, which offers tactical and saturation bombardment with matching figures

Fixes
A modded Waystation upgrade (Ashes of the Domain's Terminus) counts as the depot, so an upgraded colony is still a staging base
Marines bought at a market no longer land in your fleet as elite
LunaLib's options screen no longer crashes on a settings text with a percent sign
A hive's accessibility no longer carries vanilla's isolation penalty; density is bounded to 20 ly
A faction with no report of a found hive no longer sits out the war
A Deploy carries its hold and no longer turns back for nothing
A front no longer flaps between push and dig-in every tick
A shift fleet no longer stands on fuel it cannot pay: the passage sizes the shift

Existing saves. Saves from 0.8.2 load and carry on (tested early and deep in the war): strata, budding and the occupation start from the old garrisons, and every forward base in the save is dismantled on the first tick with its stock and marines sent home. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (forward bases off, the retired hive and council knobs dropped); values you set yourself are kept.

0.8.2 - the ground war both ways

Spoiler
Defenders get the attacker's tools: relief convoys carry marines and heavy armaments, defenders burn armaments and hold Push or Dig In stances, a convoy to a blockaded colony waits at the jump point before turning home, and stockpile marines counter-attack at full weight.
A landing under intact batteries loses troops to the guns on both sides; a front braces when beaten instead of flapping between stances; a Threat strike runs its siege by the day like an NPC siege rather than taking a world in one frame.
Both sides feed their worlds from a larder a convoy fills; the hive's stock covers a hive world's shortages of war stocks and gun inputs.
Forward bases are staging depots only, founded as needed and guarded by an escort that sails with the founding kit; the core builds up its own military and yards first instead.
Factions keep the hulls their besieged worlds' reliefs are owed from their supplies stock, commit a siege once it is a third of the way, cap a coalition's hull promise once a faction, and send coalition relief to a world with no base near it.
Fixes: the daily strike destroys forward bases again; a dry raider no longer strays between hives forever; sieges pay net of the yards they are building.

0.8.1 - hotfix
Fixed a crash when a Scouting Swarm was sent to an abyssal "Deep Space" system. Scouting Swarms now skip abyssal systems, as human scouts and Patrol Swarms already did. Saves that crashed load again.

0.8.0 - information travels by ship

Spoiler
Nobody knows anything they have not seen. No radar on either side: a hive is found when a fleet enters its system and gets home to tell of it, a siege is seen coming when a Patrol Swarm meets it and returns. The war is now fought between two AIs that both pay for everything they field, and in new-game tests at the defaults the swarm wins most sector-wide wars without the player - the core worlds hold for years, not forever. Playthroughs from 0.6 and 0.7 load and carry on (see the end).

Information and patrols
A strike no longer tells the struck faction where it came from. Factions find hives only by fleets entering the system - scouting parties, patrols, convoys, task forces - and a find counts when the party is back in a friendly system. A party destroyed on the way takes its sighting with it; a find is shared with every mobilised faction.
Both sides fly patrols from the first attack: human patrols sweep the systems around their worlds, Patrol Swarms walk the ring around each hive system and widen it as the war goes on. A patrol that meets a siege or strike force it cannot outrun is destroyed; faster and weaker it runs home with the warning; stronger it fights. Patrols grow and thin out with their losses.
The hive's distance picket and the humans' radar are gone; what each side knows is on the board as reports, and stale reports age out.
A faction mobilises only when one of its worlds is attacked - no more mobilising because the swarm is "in reach". Nobody knows of the swarm before the first attack.
Omens: foreboding messages before any hive is found - ships missing, beacons gone quiet, the fringe going dark.

The swarm attacks as a hive
Staged strikes: a strike is built from the whole hive's strike fund - a share of every hive world's production set aside for the war - at the hive world nearest the target, sized to one and a half times the defence last seen there. The war's opening strike waits until the fund can pay 8,000 FP, so the hive is strong before its first attack wakes the humans. Before, a single hive world struck with its own spare swarms, which it never had.
The nearest known target goes first, forward bases included; a forward base whose station a strike destroys is gone with it.
Strikes are no longer recalled to defend: a strike out stays out, and the system under attack defends as one, massing its spare swarms at the worlds that are short - but sends no defence it cannot win with.
The Swarm Nexus is no longer a tactical bombardment target and gives the hive no defence bonus; the swarm's stance (hold, consolidate, expand) follows the pressure on its systems.
The opening lands on a set number of home worlds (default 4). Hives cap at size 8.

The factions fight as a council
Every mobilised faction runs a strategy each month - decapitate, hold, starve and invade among them - and plays it with joint strikes, decoys and bombers, invasions once a hive's defences are down, sized from what its own ships have reported.
Forward bases: mobilised factions push chains of real outposts toward the hives they have found, and siege and hunt from them. A base builds fuel production or heavy industry by what the faction is short of, is guarded from the faction's stock, and is dismantled when nobody can pay to hold it.
Relief sails from any distance and holds the orbit over a besieged colony until the Threat army on the ground is gone, bombarding it while the defenders lose. Hunting forces that find a hive thinly held strike it instead of going home.
Human blockades of hive worlds starve them; the humans' own sieges are the cheapest first.
Once the swarm is gone from the sector every faction stands down from war footing (the player's by order only).

A closed war economy - no caps
No faction, and not the swarm, has a cap on the forces it fields: every fleet is paid for from production. Fleets out on the war's orders burn supplies upkeep and turn back when a month is owed; passage is paid in fuel on both sides; structures cost their vanilla build cost in supplies and take their vanilla build time, hive and forward base alike.
Hive worlds pay supplies upkeep by size, grow on the share they pay and shrink when starved; a hive banks its plants' and forges' output and spends the bank on swarms, founding and the strike fund. Garrisons at home pay fleet-point upkeep as the hive's patrols.
Reach is what the fuel and supplies pay for - no logistics radius anywhere. Wartime fuel and supplies bank like reserves.

Sieges and bombardment
Bombardment runs by the day: a flotilla over a hive holds the orbit while a squadron bombs, sorties are paid in fuel and supplies per day down, and saturation, tactical and siege bombardment all wear a world on the same per-day engine.
Razing disrupts and never desizes a hive; off-screen fights cost both sides.
Siege landings are sized on each hive's own floor; hunts are sized on the garrison over the world now, not a projected regrowth.

Player
Notices: every event is a titled notice with one fact a line, factions and worlds in their colours; click one to open the colony or the board.
The map fogs what you have not found; the board shows the hive systems you know and the reports your side's ships have carried home.

Fixes
A scouting party or patrol whose home world is gone (hive eradicated, forward base dismantled) no longer flies forever; it is dismissed as home.
Guards time their turn-back like a new guard; no homebound fleet leaks.
Hive fuel is back to the surplus rule by default: at the war rate the hive took the sector in one night's run.

Existing saves. Saves from 0.6 and 0.7 load (tested on a 0.6.0 and a 0.7.0 campaign, 16 and 10 years of war in). The strike fund starts empty, so the swarm's first staged strike comes four to six months after the upgrade; factions already mobilised stay so; hives already found stay found. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (Siege Orbit System off, radar settings dropped, Fabricate Troops per FP 10 to 5, Nexus Defence Bonus 0.5 to 0, Mobilise at Phase 3 to off); values you set yourself are kept.

0.7.0 - the core fights back

Spoiler
Human navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.

Hive fog of war
A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found.
The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted.
Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape.

NPC navies
Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises.
Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies.
Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size.
Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead.
Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force.

Player
Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own.
Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it.
The war board lists only the hive systems you have found, and stays off the intel list until you find the first.

Fixes
Help requests now withdraw and expire; Defend windows close.
Hive worlds no longer post survey, analyze or procurement missions.
A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full.
A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap.
Hives no longer found colonies in inhabited core systems.
NPC sieges bombard until their landing can survive the first counter-attack, and pool armaments as well as marines.
Siege landings, NPC and yours, are sized for the defences orbit can actually wear down: a hive without batteries no longer gets a landing too small to hold.
Hunting forces of hostile factions no longer meet at the same hive, and a force fights as one fleet (capped at 90 ships).
Hunts no longer spend what a base has banked for its own siege.
Your hunting fleets are no longer paid twice when you fight beside them; bounty standing comes once per battle.
Hunt is no longer offered on convoys.
Siege fleets no longer shuttle back and forth between worlds.
The disabled Aid/Defend tooltip names the real requirement: a military structure and a Waystation.

With LunaLib, the first launch moves Siege Max Fleets (10 to 25) and Mobilisation Stock (3 to 6) to the new defaults if they still hold the old ones; values you set yourself are kept.

0.6.2 - Nexerelin compatible

Spoiler
Nexerelin now works alongside the mod. Before, the mod's military-options menu replaced Nexerelin's on every world, so the Invade option never appeared.
With Nexerelin loaded, human colonies get Nexerelin's menu, Invade included. Hive worlds keep this mod's menu with Ground operations.
No Nexerelin invasion lands on a colony the swarm is besieging. The AI doesn't target it, invasion fleets already on their way are called off, and an AI ground battle already on the surface is cancelled with no change of owner. The player's Invade is greyed with the reason. It all lifts when the siege ends.
Nexerelin leaves the swarm out of its diplomacy: no peace, alliances, agents or victory count, and its own invasions and raids never target a hive.
With Nexerelin loaded, the player's tactical bombardment of a human colony is Nexerelin's version; against hives it is still the siege slice.

Fixes
Defense contracts are posted only in the name of a faction mobilised against the swarm, and an offer is withdrawn if its sponsor stands down.
Aid can be handed over through the station or base commander in the comm directory, as well as the dock menu. A contract's term now counts real days (a 120-day contract used to expire in 12).
Phase 3 ("core worlds in reach") needs a strikeable size-6+ world within the armada-capable hive's fuel range, so it is only announced when a strike could actually go there, and cutting the hive's fuel can push it back.

0.6.1 - the hive arms once it can pay

Spoiler
Fix: the hive never grew past size 3. Every hive world built its Ground Defenses at size 3, and those batteries demand metals the hive could not yet make - a size-3 world has one industry slot and Mining holds it. The unmet demand held vitality on the stall floor, so no world reached size 4, no refinery was ever built, and the whole war stayed dormant (Reach and Strikes dashed, Swarms idle). Present since 0.4.0; every save started on 0.6.0 is affected.
The hive now builds Ground Defenses and Heavy Batteries only when it can feed them - the machinery and metals they demand at least half-met, the same bar a growth input must clear. A bare mining world grows to 4, builds its refinery, and arms on the next tick.
Existing saves heal on load. A frozen hive - no refinery anywhere, size-3 worlds with batteries on the stall floor and no free slot - gets each such world the one size the freeze cost it and its production chain stood up in the same load. Expect a burst of "expanded to size 4" messages the first time you load.
The monthly sweep re-plans stalled colonies too, not only size-capped ones, and arms a world the tick it can afford to.
New debug lever, Hive Floor Size (LunaLib, Debug): grows every hive colony below a set size through the normal growth step, once per value. For catching a save up further after the freeze.

0.6.0 - the war layer

Spoiler
Threat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.

Ground war
Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.

Testing
Instant War (LunaLib, Debug): stands up a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience

Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

The Abyssal War — the Threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds.
Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.

Disclaimer: These mods were written using Claude's Fable AI model. Design and testing by pogoman.
descriptionHtml:
The Abyssal War
v0.9.2 - swarm doctrine - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8


Download

AbyssalWar-0.9.2.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves from 0.8 and 0.9 carry on; removing the mod mid-war breaks the save.


What it is
  • The Threat (vanilla's abyssal fabricator swarm) colonises the fringe of the sector, grows, and invades the core worlds
  • Its colonies are real markets with a real economy. You beat it by starving, bombing and invading them, not by killing fleets
  • The NPC factions fight it on their own. You run your own colonies' war from one intel screen (The Abyssal War)
  • Standalone. LunaLib optional. Nexerelin compatible. Safe to add mid-save

How a game goes
  • At game start a hidden fringe system is seeded with several Threat colonies ("hives"). Nobody knows
  • They grow, spread to neighbouring systems and scout the core. When they can afford a strike that beats what they saw, they attack
  • A faction whose world is struck mobilises: war economy, patrols, scouts, one big attack fleet. Factions find hives only by flying into their systems
  • You find hives the same way: fly into the system, or own a colony next door. Found hives appear on the board; the map hides the rest
  • Once you have colonies, press Mobilise on the board. Your colonies bank hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, and you spend them on orders
  • A hive dies when its strata (below) reach zero: bomb it from orbit, land marines, or cut off what feeds it. Kill every hive and the war ends
  • The core holds for years on its own and usually loses without you

The Threat, explained
  • Strata is a hive's one number. It is the colony's ground defence, its hit points and its troops at once. Fight it on the ground or bomb it from orbit, and the number goes down. Below each size's threshold the colony drops a size; at zero it is destroyed
  • Each size needs twice the strata of the last, so a size 8 hive is a fortress and a size 2 seed is nothing
  • Strata is also its fleets. A hive has no standing garrison. When attacked, or to strike, it turns strata into ships ("budding"); when the ships come home it turns them back into strata ("absorbing"). A hive that buds a defence fleet has that much less on the ground
  • Reclaimed hulls. The swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken; a fleet budded there includes those hulls, with Threat weapons, beside its own ships. A wreck also adds strata to the world
  • The Fabrication Core is the industry that makes strata. It needs metals and fuel, more of each the bigger the colony. Both met in full: the hive grows a size at a time. Short: it holds. Starved: it loses strata daily and shrinks a size at a time until it is gone
  • Hives import from each other like any market. Blockade a hive (hold its orbit with warships) and it imports nothing; only its own mines, refineries and fuel plants still feed its Core. Saturation bombardment disrupts those for a year
  • A hive's accessibility is how much strata stands nearby ("swarm density"). Dense systems grow; an isolated hive starves
  • Hives move strata between systems: back-line worlds bud fleets that fly to the front and are absorbed there. A world under attack pulls strata in. The hive's best mine, refinery and fuel plant never give strata away below their own size
  • A strike is strata too. The hive stages strata at its front worlds, grows them toward size 8, then buds the mass as one strike sized to beat the defence its scouts saw
  • Over your world the strike's ships break up into troops and land. Landed strata never come home
  • Occupation. The swarm never takes a human world. Each district its army holds lets it eat one industry: the industry stops working, is consumed over its build time and is removed. What it eats becomes strata: troops while the fight is on, then Infestation Swarms in orbit once every district is held. With nothing left to eat the army lifts off and looks for the next world

Hulls consumed by the swarm


A hive's Core fed in full: metals 3 of 3, fuel 1 of 1, 600 strata a month, the next size in 36 days.


The same hive blockaded: nothing docks, the Core gets nothing, it loses a size in 24 days.

Killing a hive
  • Find it: fly into the system. The Threat tab lists every found system nearest first, with what your last scout saw there and how old that is. Scout sends a scout from the board; Map shows the system
  • Starve it: blockade the orbit, saturation-bomb its mine, refinery or fuel plant, or kill the hive those imports come from. A seed hive dies on blockade alone
  • Bomb it: tactical bombardment from the dock razes strata for fuel. The hive buds ships from its strata to stop you; beat them first
  • Invade it: Ground operations at the dock lands all or half your marines with heavy armaments. The front fights the strata standing and keeps fighting after you leave; Push or Hold it from the board, Reinforce it, Recall evacuates it
  • Or do it all from the board: Attack on a system's row raises a fleet at your chosen colony, sized by the Fleet lever against the swarms seen there, carrying fuel and marines by the levers, and holds the system for the Days lever. It blockades, bombs while it has fuel, lands its marines on arrival and comes home when both are spent
  • Its size on the board is what your last scout saw. Nothing about a hive is live


The Threat tab: the swarm's fronts on five human worlds, and every found system nearest first with the last scout's note.


A hive system under attack: its worlds bud fleets out of their strata.

Defending your worlds
  • A colony's defence is its ground defences manned by marines, plus its spare marines armed with heavy armaments. No marines, no defence: a colony fights with what is in its stockpile
  • Marines arm over days, take losses daily while a front stands, and gain veterancy. Heavy armaments are burned per marine per day
  • The fight is one line. Each side pushes with its strength; the net moves the line; a district changes hands when it moves far enough. The board reads it from your side: gaining, grinding, losing
  • Push spends cover to move the line; Hold regrows cover. A dug-in force breaks under enough weight; an outnumbered push still gains, slower
  • Each district the swarm holds is an industry it is eating. Take the district back and the industry rebuilds from where it was. Finish eating and it is gone for good
  • Every front row says what is next (Objective), when (ETA) and when it ends (Victory). Hover for the figures each side needs
  • While the swarm holds the orbit the colony cannot dock anything; relief convoys wait at the jump point


A front on Haven: who holds what, what each side needs, what is next and when.


A colony under occupation: Farming and Mining being eaten, Ground Defenses rebuilding after its district was retaken.

Your war board
  • Mobilise puts every colony of yours on War Footing: a market condition that demands hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, so your industries bank them as the colony's stockpile. The stockpile is the reserve the board spends
  • Domain table: one row a colony with its stockpile, its fleet on station and its status. Levers above it, one per good: None / Med / Max is nothing, half or all of what the colony can spare
  • Deploy raises a fleet from a colony's hulls at the Fleet lever and sends it where you say. Transfer moves stock between your worlds by convoy. Recall brings a fleet home with what it carries. Attack (Threat tab) sends a fleet at a hive system
  • Every fleet and convoy pays fuel for the passage and burns supplies while out. It turns home when supplies run out, and its row says why
  • Call for aid on a world under attack: a toggle per good. Factions with a surplus post offers; Accept, Dismiss or Cancel. Their asks of you show the exact figure, the standing it pays and the ETA; Send or ignore
  • Defend an ally's orbit for 30 / 90 / 180 days, or send any good to any faction; standing on arrival, one rate either way
  • Outpost: dock at any uncolonised world to build one. Storage, refit, a base of your own
  • Nothing of yours moves unless you order it. No order of yours is refused
  • Every other mobilised faction has a tab: its worlds, fronts, fleets and requests, read the same way


Your tab: three factions answering Arkoman's call for marines, two fronts, and your Domain with its levers and orders.

The sector
  • A faction mobilises when one of its worlds is struck, never before. Its colonies bank the same reserves yours do
  • It attacks with one grand fleet: half its navy and every marine and fuel unit its bases can spare, to the nearest hive it outweighs. It bombs and lands until the hive is gone, moves to the next it can reach, and comes home when its holds run dry
  • Factions aid each other through the same asks and offers you see, their own colonies first
  • Every strike, grand fleet, convoy and scout is a real fleet you can meet, intercept or fight beside
  • Kill every hive and every faction stands down

Fog of war
  • No radar on either side. A hive is found when a ship sees it and gets home
  • Patrols on both sides. One that cannot outrun a strike dies with its warning
  • The board shows what your scouts reported and how old it is. The map veils what you have not found
  • The swarm only strikes worlds its own scouts have charted

Start your way
  • Default: a hive seeded on the fringe at game start, striking once it can pay
  • Chill: wake it after the Abyssal questline, or when your colony reaches size 6
  • Instant War: a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle

The settings menu (LunaLib, Shift+F2) holds the knobs that matter; the rest live in [tt]data/config/settings.json[/tt].


Changelog

0.9.2 - swarm doctrine
SpoilerThreat fleets fight by what they carry, and big swarms carry fabricators again. Saves from 0.9 carry on: fleets already flying get their fabricators on first load.

Battle doctrine by composition
  • A Threat fleet with no fabricator or hive in the battle attacks as a swarm: every combat unit aggressive, never backing off, never pulling out to vent, on search and destroy. Before, such a fleet had no orders and ended every battle pinned on its own edge
  • A fleet with a fabricator or hive deployed defends it, as vanilla
  • Swarm Doctrine, Swarm Personality (aggressive or reckless), Swarm Never Vents and Swarm Engagement Range (LunaLib)

Fabricators
  • A budded swarm (Defense and Shifting Swarms, occupation garrisons) carries one fabricator per 1,200 fleet points, at most 3, as its flagship. A fabricator is 600 FP of the fleet. A strike that musters such a swarm keeps its fabricator
  • Fleets already flying trade their smallest plain Threat hulls for the fabricators their size earns, fleet points unchanged. Converted hulls, hives and overseers are never traded
  • Fabricator Threshold (FP) and Fabricators Per Fleet (LunaLib)

Hive military options
  • Raids and bombardment of a hive close only while the swarm holds its orbit, and the menu lists every fleet holding it, so Engage can always reach what closes them. A garrison from a neighbouring moon no longer closes bombardment while the menu says there are no nearby fleets
  • The bombard tooltip shows both sides' fleet points while the orbit is held

0.9.1 - reclaimed hulls
SpoilerThe swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Saves from 0.9.0 carry on: on first load every hive world of size 5 or more gets a few hulls to start with.

Converted hulls
  • 45 vanilla warships, frigate to capital (carriers included; no phase, civilian, module or unique hulls) have a Threat version, "<Hull> (Converted)": Threat sprite and engines, the automated, Threat and fragment swarm hullmods, unboardable. Fleet points, ordnance and slots are the original's
  • 107 loadouts from vanilla's own variants, with Threat weapons in the mounts: mass drivers and the Neoferric Quadcoil in ballistic mounts, Voltaic Cannon and Voidblaster in energy, Neutron Torpedoes, Kinetic Fragments and Swarm Launchers in missile, Voltaic Discharge for point defence. Large energy, large missile and ballistic point-defence mounts keep the original weapon. Ordnance points are not a limit
  • The Threat's battle coordination counts them as combat units. Vanilla's own abyss fleets never use them
  • Converted Hulls (LunaLib) turns them off; read at game launch

The reclaimed-hull ledger
  • Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken, by type. A hull is in one place: on a ledger, or in a fleet
  • A battle the swarm wins books every hull the losers lost - yours included - to the winning swarm's world, or the nearest hive. Off-screen fights count too: ships the swarm destroys out of a fleet are booked by name; a route's or an expedition's losses are booked by type from the losing faction's known ships, cheaper types more often
  • Every hull taken adds half its fleet points as strata at the world. The swarm's own dead are not taken
  • A fleet budded or built at a world takes its converted share from that world's ledger. A world with no hulls of a class buds Threat units instead, so a young hive that has won nothing has none. Scouts and patrols never carry them
  • A converted hull absorbed back into a world goes back on the ledger; one destroyed, or landed as troops, is gone

Fleets
  • Host, Vanguard and Battery swarms spend 10-15 of 100 fleet points on converted hulls, Hunter packs 10 on converted frigates; Tide and Scout carry none
  • New Reclaimed archetype: overseers herding converted hulls of every class, 65 of 100, in the strike and garrison pools

Debug
  • Reclaimed Swarm (LunaLib, debug section): once per toggle-on, seeds every hive world's ledger with Reclaimed Seed FP of shapes and buds a Reclaimed swarm of Reclaimed Swarm FP from the hive nearest you, placed beside your fleet with orders to intercept it. Turn it off afterward

0.9.0 - strata are the Threat
SpoilerThe Threat is rebuilt around one number. Before, a hive was a vanilla-style colony with batteries, a military organ, a standing garrison of Defense Swarms and a supplies upkeep. Now a hive is its strata, and everything it does is strata changing form. Saves from 0.8.2 load and carry on (see the end).

Strata
  • A hive's strata is its ground defence, its hit points and its troops in one number, and its size is read off it: each size needs twice the strata of the last (400 at size 1). Strata lost on the ground or to bombardment lower the number; below the size's threshold the colony shrinks a size; at zero it is destroyed
  • Gone with it: hive Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, the Swarm Nexus, Bastion and Command, return fire on landings, drop losses, fortification raids, and the hive's supplies upkeep. A hive has nothing to raid
  • Nothing decays. A hive keeps what it has until something takes it

The Fabrication Core
  • The Core is the one industry that matters. It turns metals and fuel into strata daily, at a rate set by the colony's size, and demands more of each the bigger the colony (metals at size, fuel at size minus two)
  • Both inputs met in full: the hive grows, a size at a time. Either short: it holds. Both starved: it loses strata daily and drops a size at a time until it dies
  • Inputs come from the hive's own mines, refineries and fuel plants and from imports off other hives. A hive industry produces at its size
  • Blockade (hostile warships holding the orbit) cuts imports to nothing. Saturation bombardment disrupts an industry for a year, so bombing a hive's only fuel plant starves every hive that imports from it
  • Accessibility is swarm density: strata standing in and near the system. An isolated hive starves on its own; a dense cluster thrives
  • The Hive Vitality tooltip on a hive's colony screen is the readout: strata and the next size's threshold, inputs met, density or blockade, growth or days to the next size lost

Budding and absorbing
  • A hive has no standing fleets. It buds ships out of its strata when a hostile fleet holds its orbit, to strike, to shift or to seed, and absorbs them back when the job is done, one ship a tick with the break-up animation on the map
  • Absorb a fleet and the colony grows by that strata; bud one and it shrinks. A fleet is strata in space. Bombing a hive before it buds leaves it less to bud with
  • Budding and absorbing run at the world's flow (a fixed amount a day, more at big worlds), so a big fleet takes days to raise
  • Over an enemy world the swarm's ships break up into troops: a landing is strata on the ground, sized to overrun the defence, and never returns

Strata on the move
  • The shift: a world that needs strata (under attack, or at the front) is answered by the quiet world of another system that can give the most, which buds a fleet that flies there and is absorbed. Pressing, the hive shifts forward; consolidating, back toward its densest system
  • A world under attack pulls strata into its system; a system under attack never gives any away
  • Forward staging: while the hive saves for a campaign it fills its staging worlds toward size 8, then buds the mass as the strike. Strikes bud at every giver in parallel and gather at the staging system, the richest back-line worlds drawn down first
  • Critical producers keep their size: the sole largest mine, refinery or fuel plant gives nothing below its own size to a strike or a shift, since every importer's supply is read off the largest source. Its own defence may still spend everything
  • A shift books its passage fuel before it sails. Seeding a new world is strata in flight: the seed lands as a small colony and grows on its Core

Occupation, not conquest
  • The swarm never takes a human world. Its army on the ground holds districts; each district held lets it eat one industry. An eaten industry stops working at once, is consumed over its own build time (Mining 60 days, Orbital Works 150) and is then removed from the colony. Military structures are eaten last
  • What it eats becomes strata: troops to the front while districts are contested, and once every district is held a pool that buds Infestation Swarms over the world. A quiet occupation's swarms are reabsorbed; a station over the front draws the next strike
  • Take a district back and its industry is released and rebuilds from where it was eaten (it shows Rebuilding). The swarm claims the easiest to eat next; defenders reclaim military first
  • Nothing left to eat: the army lifts off and the swarm picks another world. Its final objective on a world reads Consume; yours on a hive reads Extermination
  • On the colony screen a claimed industry is tinted with the swarm's icon and a Consumed countdown; the dock is locked while the swarm holds the orbit

The line
  • One front line replaces the counter-attack cadence. Each side's pressure is its strength; the net moves the line; a district changes hands when it moves far enough. State reads from your side: gaining, grinding, losing, plus entrenched, dug in, holding, breaking, retreating, overrun
  • Push or Hold (Dig in is now Hold). Push spends cover to move the line, Hold regrows it; pressure breaks cover, so a dug-in force is breakable under enough weight and an outnumbered push gains ground in proportion. Ground taken is kept when you switch
  • Manned defences: a colony's ground defence counts only with marines to man it and takes losses like them. A colony with no marines defends with nothing
  • AI fronts push only while pushing moves the line, and hold a stance ten days before changing it
  • Fronts table: Force in each side's colour, State, Held (districts), Stance, Losses, ETA, Objective (the next district or industry), Arms, Victory, Space. The row tooltip is one line per fact: control of the district, each side's figure and what it needs, attrition, arming pace

Grand fleets (NPC offence)
  • Each faction attacks with one grand fleet. It musters half the faction's navy (floored and capped) at the base nearest the nearest known hive, loads every marine, armament and fuel unit its base and donors can spare, and sails on hulls, passage and the cruise's supplies
  • At the nearest hive it outweighs it fights what holds the orbit, razes strata with its fuel, lands its marines and stays until the hive is gone, then moves to the next hive it can reach, else home. A beaten fleet turns home and waits before trying again
  • The council's sized sieges, hunts, bombing plays and forward bases are gone. Forward bases are off by default and none are founded
  • Relief goes where the swarm is: a relief over a quiet world moves to its owner's nearest invaded world it can outweigh, or to where you are fighting
  • A faction tops up its own colonies from sibling surplus before asking the sector; all faction-to-faction aid goes through the asks and answers on the boards, free of standing between NPCs

Your board: levers and orders
  • The Min / Med / Max ladders are gone. One lever a good above each table (Fuel, Supplies, Marines, Arms, Hulls, Fleet): None / Med / Max is nothing, half or all of what the source colony can spare
  • Domain table: Colony, Size, Military, Def, Hulls, Marines, Arms, Fuel, Supplies, Strikes, Status, Fleet, Actions. Status is what the world needs. One button a row: Deploy (a fleet, with the Fleet lever set) or Transfer (a convoy), and Recall
  • Deploy raises a fleet from a colony's free hulls (the nearest colony with hulls when the row's has none), loads the levers' share of its stock, and sails where you say; Redeploy moves it on. Inside the colony's own system it is never refused for supplies. Fleets are capped at 2,400 FP each; a bigger force sails as several
  • Attack (Threat tab, each system's row): Colony picks the colony it sails from (your staging base by default), Fleet sizes it against the swarms seen there, Days sets how long it holds each world (60 / 120 / 240). The colony levers load its fuel and marines. At the target it blockades, bombs while it has fuel, lands its marines on arrival, and comes home when both are spent
  • Fronts: one stance button (Push / Hold), Reinforce at the levers, Recall sails the evacuation convoy at once, Request on your own world under a Threat army
  • Defend an ally's orbit for 30 / 90 / 180 days (Days lever), priced on the term; a defence fleet earns standing by its fleet points
  • Your orders are never gated by a front, a spare cap or a range: distance costs time and fuel. Nothing of yours moves unordered (no automatic convoys from your colonies)
  • Fleet rows show an ETA while sailing and days left once arrived; a Returning row says why; convoy rows show a blockade hold; scouts and patrols show in the fleets table

Requests and aid
  • The mission board is gone. Call for aid with a toggle per good (Fuel, Supplies, Marines, Arms, Hulls, Fleet) on a world under attack; factions look at standing calls daily
  • Offers come only from colonies with a real surplus, sized to what that colony can spare (its own siege bank held back), never to your need. Accept, Dismiss or Cancel; a faction busy with the war answers slower; a donor that needs the goods withdraws. No table shows while no offer stands
  • NPC tabs share the Requests table. A faction's ask of you shows the exact figure, sized to what you can field, the standing it pays and the ETA. Send or ignore. Left a few days, friendly factions answer it and the row logs who did
  • Standing: one rate either way, on a curve, hulls priced above armaments. Aid any non-hostile faction to raise standing. A transfer of your own landing at your own world notifies like aid
  • Strike contracts, the Hunt order and the Hive systems in reach table are gone

Convoys, fleets, performance
  • Convoys pay fuel and supplies for the voyage, yours included, billed on the hulls they sail with. A blockaded colony sends none, and a convoy to one waits at the jump point until the orbit clears
  • One fleet: every force sails as fleets of up to 2,400 FP (knob) in place of a dozen 300 FP fleets, both sides. Idle swarm fleets over a quiet world are reabsorbed
  • The LunaLib menu lists 63 knobs with a tangible effect in place of 439
  • Marines are crew first: a colony's defence counts the marines manning its ground defence, then the rest as armed troops

Information
  • The Threat tab shows what your scouts know, nothing live: Distance first, Strikes, Activity, Supply, a Notes cell from the last report ("Size 8 fuel production", "Strike staging", "Starving") with its age, and Scout, Map and Attack on every row. Mass, state, Reach and Flow are gone
  • Scouts range on their fuel and sweep found hives their faction has no report of; a lost scout is logged. The map veils found hives too (debug mode unveils it and adds a Debug tab of the swarm's plans)

Notices and the colony screen
  • Technical reports only: the war comms, the omens, hive size-change notices and AI fleet announcements are gone. Notices carry the Abyssal War intel tag and are not Major events
  • A destroyed colony's card names the destroyer. Beachhead Overrun on your world plays the mission-complete chime. The Ground War condition icon is gone from the colony screen; no Cancel upgrade on a held card
  • The hive's colony screen reads the strata: no Spaceport line, no stability lines, no human demands; the Hive Vitality tooltip is the readout
  • Player outposts: the dock offers vanilla's storage, ship transfer and refit, plus Decommission. Never mind on a hive bombardment returns to the mod's menu, which offers tactical and saturation bombardment with matching figures

Fixes
  • A modded Waystation upgrade (Ashes of the Domain's Terminus) counts as the depot, so an upgraded colony is still a staging base
  • Marines bought at a market no longer land in your fleet as elite
  • LunaLib's options screen no longer crashes on a settings text with a percent sign
  • A hive's accessibility no longer carries vanilla's isolation penalty; density is bounded to 20 ly
  • A faction with no report of a found hive no longer sits out the war
  • A Deploy carries its hold and no longer turns back for nothing
  • A front no longer flaps between push and dig-in every tick
  • A shift fleet no longer stands on fuel it cannot pay: the passage sizes the shift

Existing saves. Saves from 0.8.2 load and carry on (tested early and deep in the war): strata, budding and the occupation start from the old garrisons, and every forward base in the save is dismantled on the first tick with its stock and marines sent home. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (forward bases off, the retired hive and council knobs dropped); values you set yourself are kept.

0.8.2 - the ground war both ways
Spoiler
  • Defenders get the attacker's tools: relief convoys carry marines and heavy armaments, defenders burn armaments and hold Push or Dig In stances, a convoy to a blockaded colony waits at the jump point before turning home, and stockpile marines counter-attack at full weight.
  • A landing under intact batteries loses troops to the guns on both sides; a front braces when beaten instead of flapping between stances; a Threat strike runs its siege by the day like an NPC siege rather than taking a world in one frame.
  • Both sides feed their worlds from a larder a convoy fills; the hive's stock covers a hive world's shortages of war stocks and gun inputs.
  • Forward bases are staging depots only, founded as needed and guarded by an escort that sails with the founding kit; the core builds up its own military and yards first instead.
  • Factions keep the hulls their besieged worlds' reliefs are owed from their supplies stock, commit a siege once it is a third of the way, cap a coalition's hull promise once a faction, and send coalition relief to a world with no base near it.
  • Fixes: the daily strike destroys forward bases again; a dry raider no longer strays between hives forever; sieges pay net of the yards they are building.

0.8.1 - hotfix
  • Fixed a crash when a Scouting Swarm was sent to an abyssal "Deep Space" system. Scouting Swarms now skip abyssal systems, as human scouts and Patrol Swarms already did. Saves that crashed load again.

0.8.0 - information travels by ship
SpoilerNobody knows anything they have not seen. No radar on either side: a hive is found when a fleet enters its system and gets home to tell of it, a siege is seen coming when a Patrol Swarm meets it and returns. The war is now fought between two AIs that both pay for everything they field, and in new-game tests at the defaults the swarm wins most sector-wide wars without the player - the core worlds hold for years, not forever. Playthroughs from 0.6 and 0.7 load and carry on (see the end).

Information and patrols
  • A strike no longer tells the struck faction where it came from. Factions find hives only by fleets entering the system - scouting parties, patrols, convoys, task forces - and a find counts when the party is back in a friendly system. A party destroyed on the way takes its sighting with it; a find is shared with every mobilised faction.
  • Both sides fly patrols from the first attack: human patrols sweep the systems around their worlds, Patrol Swarms walk the ring around each hive system and widen it as the war goes on. A patrol that meets a siege or strike force it cannot outrun is destroyed; faster and weaker it runs home with the warning; stronger it fights. Patrols grow and thin out with their losses.
  • The hive's distance picket and the humans' radar are gone; what each side knows is on the board as reports, and stale reports age out.
  • A faction mobilises only when one of its worlds is attacked - no more mobilising because the swarm is "in reach". Nobody knows of the swarm before the first attack.
  • Omens: foreboding messages before any hive is found - ships missing, beacons gone quiet, the fringe going dark.
The swarm attacks as a hive
  • Staged strikes: a strike is built from the whole hive's strike fund - a share of every hive world's production set aside for the war - at the hive world nearest the target, sized to one and a half times the defence last seen there. The war's opening strike waits until the fund can pay 8,000 FP, so the hive is strong before its first attack wakes the humans. Before, a single hive world struck with its own spare swarms, which it never had.
  • The nearest known target goes first, forward bases included; a forward base whose station a strike destroys is gone with it.
  • Strikes are no longer recalled to defend: a strike out stays out, and the system under attack defends as one, massing its spare swarms at the worlds that are short - but sends no defence it cannot win with.
  • The Swarm Nexus is no longer a tactical bombardment target and gives the hive no defence bonus; the swarm's stance (hold, consolidate, expand) follows the pressure on its systems.
  • The opening lands on a set number of home worlds (default 4). Hives cap at size 8.
The factions fight as a council
  • Every mobilised faction runs a strategy each month - decapitate, hold, starve and invade among them - and plays it with joint strikes, decoys and bombers, invasions once a hive's defences are down, sized from what its own ships have reported.
  • Forward bases: mobilised factions push chains of real outposts toward the hives they have found, and siege and hunt from them. A base builds fuel production or heavy industry by what the faction is short of, is guarded from the faction's stock, and is dismantled when nobody can pay to hold it.
  • Relief sails from any distance and holds the orbit over a besieged colony until the Threat army on the ground is gone, bombarding it while the defenders lose. Hunting forces that find a hive thinly held strike it instead of going home.
  • Human blockades of hive worlds starve them; the humans' own sieges are the cheapest first.
  • Once the swarm is gone from the sector every faction stands down from war footing (the player's by order only).
A closed war economy - no caps
  • No faction, and not the swarm, has a cap on the forces it fields: every fleet is paid for from production. Fleets out on the war's orders burn supplies upkeep and turn back when a month is owed; passage is paid in fuel on both sides; structures cost their vanilla build cost in supplies and take their vanilla build time, hive and forward base alike.
  • Hive worlds pay supplies upkeep by size, grow on the share they pay and shrink when starved; a hive banks its plants' and forges' output and spends the bank on swarms, founding and the strike fund. Garrisons at home pay fleet-point upkeep as the hive's patrols.
  • Reach is what the fuel and supplies pay for - no logistics radius anywhere. Wartime fuel and supplies bank like reserves.
Sieges and bombardment
  • Bombardment runs by the day: a flotilla over a hive holds the orbit while a squadron bombs, sorties are paid in fuel and supplies per day down, and saturation, tactical and siege bombardment all wear a world on the same per-day engine.
  • Razing disrupts and never desizes a hive; off-screen fights cost both sides.
  • Siege landings are sized on each hive's own floor; hunts are sized on the garrison over the world now, not a projected regrowth.
Player
  • Notices: every event is a titled notice with one fact a line, factions and worlds in their colours; click one to open the colony or the board.
  • The map fogs what you have not found; the board shows the hive systems you know and the reports your side's ships have carried home.
Fixes
  • A scouting party or patrol whose home world is gone (hive eradicated, forward base dismantled) no longer flies forever; it is dismissed as home.
  • Guards time their turn-back like a new guard; no homebound fleet leaks.
  • Hive fuel is back to the surplus rule by default: at the war rate the hive took the sector in one night's run.
Existing saves. Saves from 0.6 and 0.7 load (tested on a 0.6.0 and a 0.7.0 campaign, 16 and 10 years of war in). The strike fund starts empty, so the swarm's first staged strike comes four to six months after the upgrade; factions already mobilised stay so; hives already found stay found. With LunaLib, the first launch moves changed defaults to the new values if they still hold the old ones (Siege Orbit System off, radar settings dropped, Fabricate Troops per FP 10 to 5, Nexus Defence Bonus 0.5 to 0, Mobilise at Phase 3 to off); values you set yourself are kept.

0.7.0 - the core fights back
