SpoilerHuman navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.

Hive fog of war
  • A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found.
  • The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted.
  • Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape.
NPC navies
  • Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises.
  • Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies.
  • Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size.
  • Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead.
  • Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force.
Player
  • Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own.
  • Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it.
  • The war board lists only the hive systems you have found, and stays off the intel list until you find the first.
Fixes
  • Help requests now withdraw and expire; Defend windows close.
  • Hive worlds no longer post survey, analyze or procurement missions.
  • A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full.
  • A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap.
  • Hives no longer found colonies in inhabited core systems.
  • NPC sieges bombard until their landing can survive the first counter-attack, and pool armaments as well as marines.
  • Siege landings, NPC and yours, are sized for the defences orbit can actually wear down: a hive without batteries no longer gets a landing too small to hold.
  • Hunting forces of hostile factions no longer meet at the same hive, and a force fights as one fleet (capped at 90 ships).
  • Hunts no longer spend what a base has banked for its own siege.
  • Your hunting fleets are no longer paid twice when you fight beside them; bounty standing comes once per battle.
  • Hunt is no longer offered on convoys.
  • Siege fleets no longer shuttle back and forth between worlds.
  • The disabled Aid/Defend tooltip names the real requirement: a military structure and a Waystation.
With LunaLib, the first launch moves Siege Max Fleets (10 to 25) and Mobilisation Stock (3 to 6) to the new defaults if they still hold the old ones; values you set yourself are kept.
0.6.2 - Nexerelin compatible
SpoilerNexerelin now works alongside the mod. Before, the mod's military-options menu replaced Nexerelin's on every world, so the Invade option never appeared.
  • With Nexerelin loaded, human colonies get Nexerelin's menu, Invade included. Hive worlds keep this mod's menu with Ground operations.
  • No Nexerelin invasion lands on a colony the swarm is besieging. The AI doesn't target it, invasion fleets already on their way are called off, and an AI ground battle already on the surface is cancelled with no change of owner. The player's Invade is greyed with the reason. It all lifts when the siege ends.
  • Nexerelin leaves the swarm out of its diplomacy: no peace, alliances, agents or victory count, and its own invasions and raids never target a hive.
  • With Nexerelin loaded, the player's tactical bombardment of a human colony is Nexerelin's version; against hives it is still the siege slice.
Fixes
  • Defense contracts are posted only in the name of a faction mobilised against the swarm, and an offer is withdrawn if its sponsor stands down.
  • Aid can be handed over through the station or base commander in the comm directory, as well as the dock menu. A contract's term now counts real days (a 120-day contract used to expire in 12).
  • Phase 3 ("core worlds in reach") needs a strikeable size-6+ world within the armada-capable hive's fuel range, so it is only announced when a strike could actually go there, and cutting the hive's fuel can push it back.
0.6.1 - the hive arms once it can pay
SpoilerFix: the hive never grew past size 3. Every hive world built its Ground Defenses at size 3, and those batteries demand metals the hive could not yet make - a size-3 world has one industry slot and Mining holds it. The unmet demand held vitality on the stall floor, so no world reached size 4, no refinery was ever built, and the whole war stayed dormant (Reach and Strikes dashed, Swarms idle). Present since 0.4.0; every save started on 0.6.0 is affected.
  • The hive now builds Ground Defenses and Heavy Batteries only when it can feed them - the machinery and metals they demand at least half-met, the same bar a growth input must clear. A bare mining world grows to 4, builds its refinery, and arms on the next tick.
  • Existing saves heal on load. A frozen hive - no refinery anywhere, size-3 worlds with batteries on the stall floor and no free slot - gets each such world the one size the freeze cost it and its production chain stood up in the same load. Expect a burst of "expanded to size 4" messages the first time you load.
  • The monthly sweep re-plans stalled colonies too, not only size-capped ones, and arms a world the tick it can afford to.
  • New debug lever, Hive Floor Size (LunaLib, Debug): grows every hive colony below a set size through the normal growth step, once per value. For catching a save up further after the freeze.
0.6.0 - the war layer
SpoilerThreat Incursion is now The Abyssal War. The mod id is unchanged, so existing saves keep working.

Ground war
  • Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
  • Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
  • Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
  • Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
  • Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
  • Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
  • Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
  • Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
  • A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
  • Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
  • The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
  • NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
  • Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
  • Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
  • Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
  • Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
  • Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
  • Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
  • Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
  • Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
  • NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
  • Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
  • Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
  • Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
  • Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
  • A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
  • War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
  • Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
  • Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
  • Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
  • Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
  • Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
  • A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
  • Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
  • Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.

Board
  • Ground Fronts table, per system, with order buttons on every front.
  • Per-fleet rows with Recall and Intercept.
  • Colony rows open vanilla's own colony screen.
  • Purge commissions removed; sieges launch from the faction view.
  • Tooltips rewritten: one line per fact, and every button says what pressing it does - or why it cannot be pressed.
  • The intel list row reads at vanilla's own size now, next to Colony Crises.

Testing
  • Instant War (LunaLib, Debug): stands up a mature sector-wide war on a fresh save in one toggle.

Recommended mod collection for ultimate late game experience
Standalone, safe to add mid-save, can be run together or separately.

  • The Abyssal War — the Threat colonizes the sector and invades the core worlds.
  • Remnant Retribution — a late-game colony crisis.
  • Commerce Wars — dominate a faction's markets or the military balance and they push back: ultimatums, tribute, enforcement fleets.
  • Piracy Reworked — the underworld runs on your money: black-market trade funds a self-sustaining pirate war economy.

changelog.0.9.2:
swarm doctrine - for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

 Download

AbyssalWar-0.9.2.zip

Extract into your Starsector mods/ folder and enable it in the launcher. It extracts to mods/ThreatIncursion - overwrite your existing folder rather than keeping both. Saves from 0.8 and 0.9 carry on; removing the mod mid-war breaks the save.

 What it is
 The Threat (vanilla's abyssal fabricator swarm) colonises the fringe of the sector, grows, and invades the core worlds
 Its colonies are real markets with a real economy. You beat it by starving, bombing and invading them, not by killing fleets
 The NPC factions fight it on their own. You run your own colonies' war from one intel screen (The Abyssal War)
 Standalone. LunaLib optional. Nexerelin compatible. Safe to add mid-save

 How a game goes
 At game start a hidden fringe system is seeded with several Threat colonies ("hives"). Nobody knows
 They grow, spread to neighbouring systems and scout the core. When they can afford a strike that beats what they saw, they attack
 A faction whose world is struck mobilises: war economy, patrols, scouts, one big attack fleet. Factions find hives only by flying into their systems
 You find hives the same way: fly into the system, or own a colony next door. Found hives appear on the board; the map hides the rest
 Once you have colonies, press Mobilise on the board. Your colonies bank hulls, marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies, and you spend them on orders
 A hive dies when its strata (below) reach zero: bomb it from orbit, land marines, or cut off what feeds it. Kill every hive and the war ends
 The core holds for years on its own and usually loses without you

 The Threat, explained
 Strata is a hive's one number. It is the colony's ground defence, its hit points and its troops at once. Fight it on the ground or bomb it from orbit, and the number goes down. Below each size's threshold the colony drops a size; at zero it is destroyed
 Each size needs twice the strata of the last, so a size 8 hive is a fortress and a size 2 seed is nothing
 Strata is also its fleets. A hive has no standing garrison. When attacked, or to strike, it turns strata into ships ("budding"); when the ships come home it turns them back into strata ("absorbing"). A hive that buds a defence fleet has that much less on the ground
 Reclaimed hulls. The swarm consumes and repurposes the fleets it destroys. Each hive world keeps a count of the hulls it has taken; a fleet budded there includes those hulls, with Threat weapons, beside its own ships. A wreck also adds strata to the world
 The Fabrication Core is the industry that makes strata. It needs metals and fuel, more of each the bigger the colony. Both met in full: the hive grows a size at a time. Short: it holds. Starved: it loses strata daily and shrinks a size at a time until it is gone
 Hives import from each other like any market. Blockade a hive (hold its orbit with warships) and it imports nothing; only its own mines, refineries and fuel plants still feed its Core. Saturation bombardment disrupts those for a year
 A hive's accessibility is how much strata stands nearby ("swarm density"). Dense systems grow; an isolated hive starves
 Hives move strata between systems: back-line worlds bud fleets that fly to the front and are absorbed there. A world under attack pulls strata in. The hive's best mine, refinery and fuel plant never give strata away below their own size
 A strike is strata too. The hive stages strata at its front worlds, grows them toward size 8, then buds the mass as one strike sized to beat the defence its scouts saw
 Over your world the strike's ships break up into troops and land. Landed strata never come home
 Occupation. The swarm never takes a human world. Each district its army holds lets it eat one industry: the industry stops working, is consumed over its build time and is removed. What it eats becomes strata: troops while the fight is on, then Infestation Swarms in orbit once every district is held. With nothing left to eat the army lifts off and looks for the next world

 Hulls consumed by the swarm

releases.changelogNotes: The Threat is rebuilt around one number. Before, a hive was a vanilla-style colony with batteries, a military organ, a standing garrison of Defense Swarms and a supplies upkeep. Now a hive is its strata, and everything it does is strata changing form. Saves from 0.8.2 load and carry on (see the end).

releases.changelogNotes: Fixed a crash when a Scouting Swarm was sent to an abyssal "Deep Space" system. Scouting Swarms now skip abyssal systems, as human scouts and Patrol Swarms already did. Saves that crashed load again.

Human navies now open the war at full strength and win early ground victories. In testing they burned 10 hive worlds in the first two years, where before they burned one in five; the hive still grinds them down if the player stays out.

Hive fog of war
A strike no longer reveals where it came from. The struck faction gets a lead and sends scouting parties to sweep the systems around it. Sieges, task forces and contracts act only on hives someone has found.
The swarm scouts too: it only strikes worlds its Scouting Swarms have charted.
Fleet archetypes: 12 new Threat variants, and strike, garrison, seeding and scout swarms are each built to their own shape.
NPC navies
Depots fill from the war's supply (importers used to bank nothing once mobilised) and start full the moment a faction mobilises.
Sieges actually launch: staging bases bank toward the siege, and convoys carry full loads of marines, fuel and supplies.
Sieges sail at full strength and weigh the Defense Swarms first. A base the swarms outweigh posts a swarm bounty, paid per Threat ship by hull size.
Landings are sized to survive the hive's first counter-attack, with marines pooled from the faction's other bases. When the nearest base cannot pay for a siege, the next nearest sails instead.
Hunting forces: a base with no siege of its own hunts a bountied hive's Defense Swarms. Fleets from every base in reach muster outside the system and go in as one fleet. Allies answer a siege call with a hunting force.
Player
Hunt replaces Intercept: send a task force to hunt a hive's Defense Swarms from the board. Your hunting fleets collect swarm bounties on their own.
Raid the fortifications: a colony's Ground Defenses, Heavy Batteries, Patrol HQ, Military Base and High Command are on the Disrupt raid list at Heavy danger. Raids wear them down past the orbital floor, and every raid's days count in full. Committing many marines to one structure costs more against a strong garrison, so several shallow raids beat one deep one. Off with Nexerelin, whose own bombardment covers it.

A hunting force that never fights gets its fuel and supplies back in full.
A swarm out raiding or reinforcing keeps its slot at home, so garrisons no longer overshoot the cap.

Ground war
Eradication is a ground campaign, not a decline timer: land marines, take the strata, kill the Fabrication Core.
Ground fronts push, dig in or withdraw; armaments burn per marine per day, so what a front carries is how long it lasts.
Fronts push the moment troops land at holding strength; a dug-in front stays dug in until the next landing.
Sieges fight for the orbit first. Bombardment wears fortification to a floor and no further - a front on the ground takes it the rest of the way.
Threat strikes land fronts of their own on inhabited worlds, dig in, then make a final push.
Colony defense is garrison troops times fortification, each worn down separately, with an orbital floor under the structures.
Marines arm over weeks, take casualties, count toward counter-attacks, and carry veterancy both ways with your fleet's marine pool.
Support and Defend fleet orders: hold the orbit, run the siege slice, or fight only while the front cannot hold.
A Defend fleet at the orbital floor can break up its own hulls into troops for the front.
Planetary shields buy real cover against orbital bombardment.
The hive scours an unopposed enemy front after three days.

Strategy layer
NPC factions enter war mode when the Threat strikes them; you mobilise or stand down yourself.
Every colony banks a visible reserve of marines, heavy armaments, fuel and supplies.
Convoys carry that stock physically - escort them, or let the swarm's raiders have them.
Fleet orders from the board: guard, stage, intercept, support, defend, siege, recall.
Guarding your own colony stages the fleet there: its strength counts at the host and folds into sorties.
Faction view shows any mobilised faction's colonies, reserves and fleets, with a totals row and a colour key.
Min / Med / Max load ladders on sieges, supply runs and convoy loads.
Recalled and expired fleets sail home and return their surviving cargo.
Sieges are leashed to the contested orbit; strays are recalled instead of chasing across the sector.

Player aid and outposts
NPC factions are autonomous now: you aid them, you do not command them.
Send Defend, Resupply, Reinforce or Strike from your own colonies, gated by a capacity ledger and reserve stock, earning standing on arrival.
Factions post their needs as ordinary missions - deliver by colony fleet, or in person at the dock.
Allies send each other aid by standing, without you.
Build an outpost over any uncolonised world, or take one free by ground victory. Dock at it for storage, or decommission it.
A later colony on that world inherits the outpost.

Economy
War reserves are the colony's real resource stockpile, not a separate hidden ledger.
Mobilised colonies carry the War Footing condition, so the war shows as genuine demand and a real shortage on the colony screen.
Depots cover the colony's own shortages before they fund anything else.
Convoys land as trade at the receiving colony.
Bases need a Waystation; NPC mobilisation builds them.

Escalation
Grudge and alarm: the swarm answers whoever hurts it most, and alarm speeds hive fabrication.
A ground victory draws retaliation from the nearest hive.
Coalition fleets answer a mobilised faction's call during a siege.
Defense Swarms detach to raid convoys, then return to their garrison.
